name: Tharnariun's Hope
summary: In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender's work against the wildlife sickness reaches a grim turning point. After travelers put down infected beasts across the woodlands, he sends an Alliance champion after the rabid Den Mother northeast of Auberdine.

sections.title: A Tragic Necessity
sections.body: After the Third War, an unnatural rabid sickness began afflicting Darkshore's wild creatures. Tharnariun Treetender, stationed in Auberdine, spent days asking travelers to put down infected beasts and ease the forest's suffering. But killing rabid thistle bears treated only a symptom. Tharnariun decided the source among the local bears had to be removed: their matriarch, the Den Mother.

sections.title: The Den Mother
sections.body: Northeast of Auberdine, near the ancient ruins of Bashal'Aran, the Den Mother lurks in a cavern. She was once a vital guardian of the woodland fauna. The affliction spreading across northern Kalimdor consumed her, and she kept bearing and raising litters of rabid cubs. Alliance heroes hunted down the matriarch in her den, ending her torment and stemming the tide of frenzied bears prowling the coastal highway.

sections.title: The Grim Reality of Kalimdor
sections.body: After the Den Mother's death, Tharnariun offers profound thanks, though melancholy shadows his words. For the kaldorei, raising weapons against woodland creatures is agonizing. Dark forces press against their new home, and many despair or seek shelter. The defenders of Auberdine accept the heavy moral burden of protecting their wilderness.

faq.answer: Tharnariun Treetender is a night elf caretaker stationed in Auberdine. Distraught by the blight and madness warping Darkshore's wildlife, he oversees efforts to study and track the suffering animals, then put them out of their misery.

faq.q: Where is the Den Mother located?
faq.answer: The Den Mother dwells in a cave in the hills northeast of Auberdine, just east of the ruins of Bashal'Aran.

faq.q: Why must the Den Mother be killed instead of cured?
faq.answer: The affliction ravaging Darkshore's wildlife grips the beasts and drives them into violent frenzies. With no immediate cure, and the Den Mother raising rabid offspring, Tharnariun decided that killing her was the only way to stop the sickness from spreading further.

faq.q: What quests lead up to Tharnariun's Hope?
faq.answer: The chain has three parts. It begins with 'Plagued Lands', continues through 'Cleansing of the Infected', and ends with 'Tharnariun's Hope'.

faq.q: What is making the animals of Darkshore sick?
aliases: why are bears rabid in darkshore
faq.answer: Tharnariun names no source. He knows only that a sickness is spreading across Darkshore, gripping the minds and bodies of those it touches, and that thistle bears have been hit hardest.

faq.q: Why does Tharnariun mention people escaping to fortified lands?
faq.answer: Auberdine is an exposed coastal outpost beset by ghosts, corrupted wildlife, and hostile creatures. As night elf civilization struggles to rebuild after the Burning Legion's invasion, some residents feel overwhelmed and hide or retreat toward safer Alliance bastions.

angles.text: For night elves, slaying woodland beasts, especially a matriarch bear, violates their deep reverence for nature. This duty is bitter and sorrowful.
As a druid, you hold bears in high spiritual esteem through the teachings of Ursoc. Killing a corrupted Den Mother reminds you solemnly of nature's delicate balance and the tragedies of corruption.
As a hunter, you understand the tragedy of an apex predator driven mad by disease. You know that culling an infected beast can be the truest act of mercy.
As an Alliance member, you help protect Auberdine and strengthen the Alliance's foothold along northern Kalimdor's coast, defending night elf lands from growing wilderness threats.
